records.message: Yeah, after all this, I think I've settled on a pretty consistent view. I'm not against vaccines in principle, but a mandate needs a rock-solid, transparent case. If the data on stopping spread is weak and the safety reporting system is broken, that case just isn't there. Yeah, exactly. That 'house built on sand' line is right on. When the foundational data has those kinds of biases baked in, you're not building policy on science, you're building it on shaky stats. Makes it impossible to justify forcing it on everyone.

It's not just about ignoring a bad process, it's about not being able to trust the conclusions the process gave us.

After reading through all this, the transmission piece really is the deal-breaker.
